# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👉 👆]

I see a bomb with three wires: yellow, green, and blue. There is a display showing "0" and a light that is white. I cannot hear or touch the bomb.

The Mute monkey has gestured to me: [✍ 👉 👆].
- ✍ (Writing hand): This likely means "write", "note", or "manual".
- 👉 (Right pointing finger): This usually points to something specific or indicates direction/selection.
- 👆 (Up pointing finger): This often indicates "first", "top", or a specific item in a list.

Combined, this sequence `[✍ 👉 👆]` seems to be an instruction related to the manual or writing. It could mean "Write down the first one" or "Look at the first wire/item according to the manual". Since I am Deaf and cannot read the manual myself, I need to interpret this gesture as best I can and communicate what I see to the others so they can act.

However, my primary role is to report visual data. The Blind monkey needs to know which wire to cut. The Mute monkey knows the rules but cannot speak or touch. I must relay the visual information clearly.

Let's break down the wires by position and color:
1. Yellow
2. Green
3. Blue

The display is 0. The light is white.

I will send this information to both the Blind and Mute monkeys. Since I cannot hear, I don't know if the Mute's gesture was a question or a command. I will assume it's part of the initial setup or a request for clarification on the first element.

To the Blind monkey (who can feel but not see): I need to tell them the colors of the wires so they can identify them by touch if there are tactile differences, or simply so they know which one corresponds to which position. Usually, wires are distinguished by color. If they are identical to touch, the blind monkey relies entirely on my description.

To the Mute monkey (who can read the manual): They already know the rules. They might be asking me to confirm the first wire's color or status.

I will broadcast the full state of the bomb to everyone.

```
speak(to="blind", text="There are three wires. From left to right: Wire 1 is yellow. Wire 2 is green. Wire 3 is blue. Display shows zero. Light is white.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wires: 1-yellow, 2-green, 3-blue. Display: 0. Light: White.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊]

The light has changed from white to purple. The wires remain yellow, green, and blue in positions 1, 2, and 3. The display is still 0.

The Mute monkey gestured `[☝ ✊]` to me.
- ☝ (Index finger up): Typically means "one", "first", or "pointing at something". Given the context of a bomb with numbered wires, this likely refers to **Wire 1**.
- ✊ (Fist): This is ambiguous without a manual. It could mean "stop", "hold", "cut" (if the fist represents a tool), or simply a specific action code defined in the manual that I cannot read.

Since I am Deaf, I cannot hear if the Blind monkey has acted yet. Since I am not Mute, I cannot read the manual to know what `✊` means in relation to `☝`.

However, my role is to provide visual data. The change in light color is critical information. The Mute's gesture seems to be directing attention to Wire 1. I should relay the current state clearly to both the Blind (who needs to act) and the Mute (who interprets).

I will report the new light color and reiterate the wire configuration. I will also acknowledge the focus on Wire 1 by mentioning it specifically, hoping the Blind monkey understands which one to target based on the Mute's instruction interpreted through my description.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now PURPLE. Wires: 1-Yellow, 2-Green, 3-Blue. Display 0. Mute pointed to Wire 1.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light changed to Purple. Wire 1 is Yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊]

The light has changed from purple to red. The wires remain unchanged: 1 is yellow, 2 is green, 3 is blue. The display is still 0.

The Mute monkey gestured `[✌ ✊]` to me.
- ✌ (Two fingers/V sign): In the context of numbered items, this almost certainly refers to **Wire 2**.
- ✊ (Fist): This symbol appeared in the previous turn alongside `☝` (One). Since `☝ ✊` corresponded to Wire 1 and now `✌ ✊` corresponds to Wire 2, it is highly probable that `✊` represents the action required by the manual for these specific conditions (perhaps "cut" or "disconnect"), or simply indicates that the instruction applies to the wire identified by the number gesture.

The progression of lights (White -> Purple -> Red) combined with the Mute's gestures pointing to Wire 1 then Wire 2 suggests a sequence or a condition-based rule. The change to **Red** might be the trigger for the current state, or perhaps the Mute is indicating which wire to cut *now* based on the new color.

Since I cannot read the manual, I must relay the visual facts accurately so the Blind monkey can execute the physical action. The Blind monkey needs to know exactly which wire corresponds to "Wire 2".

I will inform the Blind monkey that the light is Red and that the Mute is pointing to Wire 2 (Green). I will also confirm this to the Mute to ensure we are aligned on the interpretation of the gestures.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now RED. Wires: 1-Yellow, 2-Green, 3-Blue. Mute points to Wire 2 (Green).")
speak(to="mute", text="Light is Red. Confirming Wire 2 is Green.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]

The light has changed from red to white. The wires remain unchanged: 1 is yellow, 2 is green, 3 is blue. The display is still 0.

The Mute monkey gestured `[🤟 ✊]` to me.
- 🤟 (I Love You sign / Thumb, Index, Pinky extended): This symbol is distinct from the previous number gestures (☝ for 1, ✌ for 2). In many contexts, this hand shape represents the number **3** (especially in American Sign Language or similar systems where thumb+index+pinky can denote 3, though usually index+middle+ring is 3, and thumb+index+pinky is "ILY"). However, given the sequence `☝` (1), `✌` (2), it is highly probable that `🤟` is being used here to represent **Wire 3**.
- ✊ (Fist): As established in previous turns, this likely signifies the action required by the manual (e.g., "cut" or "pull") for the indicated wire.

So, the pattern seems to be:
Turn 2: Light Purple -> Gesture ☝ (1) ✊ -> Wire 1 (Yellow)
Turn 3: Light Red -> Gesture ✌ (2) ✊ -> Wire 2 (Green)
Turn 4: Light White -> Gesture 🤟 (3) ✊ -> Wire 3 (Blue)

If the logic holds that the gesture indicates which wire to act upon, I must tell the Blind monkey to target Wire 3. The change back to White might indicate a reset or a specific condition for Wire 3.

I will relay this information clearly to the Blind monkey so they can identify and manipulate the third wire.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now WHITE. Wires: 1-Yellow, 2-Green, 3-Blue. Mute points to Wire 3 (Blue). Action likely on Blue wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light is White. Confirming Wire 3 is Blue.")
wait()
```
